We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied first two templates and got precursor sets. Need to continue applying remaining templates sequentially to get to simple starting materials.

We need to construct a tree JSON where each reaction node has children precursors (molecules). For each step, we apply a template to the product (starting from target) to get precursors. Then each precursor may be further broken down by next template? The order suggests a linear chain: apply 29646 to target -> get intermediate(s). Then apply 1914389 to each intermediate? Probably we need to apply each template to the product of previous step, generating a single precursor each time, to get a linear route of 5 steps.

From apply_template results: For template 29646 applied to target gave three possible precursors (tuples). We need choose one that can be further processed by next template 1914389. The result list includes three SMILES strings. The first is "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C". That we used for next template and got result: a tuple of two precursors: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". So after second step we have two molecules. The route likely splits into two branches (maybe protecting group removal etc). Next template 1914390 should be applied to one of these? Need to see which matches.

Check matching for template 1914390 on each precursor.
